Q: Removing duplicates in a sequence A:

You can add "StartDate" to PARTITION BY

WITH CTE AS(
 SELECT *,
    RowNum = ROW_NUMBER()OVER(PARTITION BY DebtId, AgreementId,StartDate ORDER BY StartDate)
 FROM DebtHistory
)
DELETE FROM CTE WHERE RowNum > 1

Also, I suggest using a combination of the dense_rank() and row_number() functions to determine the rows to be deleted.

WITH CTE AS(
   SELECT *,
       ROW_NUMBER()OVER(PARTITION BY DebtId, AgreementId,StartDate,rnk ORDER BY rnk ) as RowNum 
   FROM (SELECT *,
          Rnk = DENSE_RANK()OVER(PARTITION BY DebtId, AgreementId ORDER BY StartDate)
        FROM DebtHistory
     )x
)
DELETE FROM CTE WHERE RowNum > 1

Q: Should I use ETC/Zulu or Zulu? A:

Neither. That page clearly warns that :

Please do not use any of the timezones listed here (besides UTC), they only exist for backward compatible reasons

You shouldn't just default to UTC, especially if you try to create an airline system. Flights use local airport time and you can't recover local time for future dates from just UTC and the local timezone. Timezone rules can change easily, but the flight times will remain the same. If you only store UTC you'll have to find and modify all affected flight times.

Not good. Some years ago, Russia changed its daylight rules 2 or three times in a couple of years. Egypt did the same with a couple of months notice. If airlines and travel agencies stored UTC, they'd have to find and modify all affected records.

Hint: I work for a big OTA (Online Travel Agency). We don't store UTC only. We store local airport time along with the airport's IANA timezone name. Airlines don't publish flights with UTC times either, they publish local airport time (along with datetime+offset and UTC conversions for convenience). Your ticket is issued for a specific local time too, not UTC.

Jon Skeet wrote Storing UTC is not a silver bullet, using both Flights and Conferences to demonstrate the problems with storing UTC and converting, before explaining why Local+Timezone with on-the-fly conversion to UTC is the best option.
